summary: Zsóka Gelle is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Berzsenyi Dániel Teacher Training College, Eötvös Loránd University, Manjushree Centre, and the University of Vienna. She held positions at Vienna, Eötvös Loránd University, and Dharma Gate Buddhist College.
Zuicho Tachibana was an archaeologist and scholar of Central Asian and Buddhist studies. He studied under Kozui Otani around 1903 and under Edward Denison Ross between circa 1908 and 1910.

Zuiei Ito (1942–2020) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Waseda University and the University of Tokyo. He taught at Shinshu, Waseda, and Tokyo universities, and served as a professor at Rissho University (1980–2013).

Zuigan Goto (1879–1965) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the Second Higher School, the University of Tokyo, and under Sokatsu Shaku. In 1932, he served as president of Hanazono University.

Zuiho Yamaguchi (1926–2023) studied at the University of Tokyo and EPHE under Jacques Bacot and Rolf Alfred Stein. Specializing in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, he held posts at CNRS, Toyo Bunko, the University of Tokyo, and Nagoya University.

Zuiryu Nakamura (1915–1997) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under Kenryu Tsukinowa and Susumu Yamaguchi. In 1945, he became a professor in the Department of Buddhist Studies at Rissho University.
Gyurme tubten nyinje studied under Shechen Gyaltsab and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.
Pad+ma la studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Dudjom Rinpoche.

Édouard Chavannes (1865–1918) was a sinologist who studied at ENS, INALCO, and Collège de France under Marquis d'Hervey de Saint-Denys and Maurice Jametel. He was a professor at Collège de France (1893–1918) and president of AIBL (1915).

Édouard Huber (1879–1914) was a scholar of sinology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at the Sorbonne, Collège de France, and other Paris institutions under Sylvain Lévi and Johann Baptist Schibenegg, and directed a department at EFEO (1901–1905).
Élisée Reclus (1830–1905) studied at the Faculté libre de théologie protestante de Montauban from 1848 to 1849 and held a post at the New University of Brussels from circa 1894 to 1905.

Émile Benveniste (1902–1976) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Paris and EPHE under Antoine Meillet and Joseph Vendryes. He served as directeur d’études at EPHE and held the Chair of Comparative Grammar at Collège de France.
Émile Chartier (1868–1951) was a philosopher who studied at Lycée Pierre-Corneille from circa 1881 to 1886 and at École Normale Supérieure from circa 1889 to 1892.

Émile Chatelain (1851–1933) was a scholar of linguistics and archaeology who studied at École Pratique des Hautes Études. He held positions at the École française de Rome (1876–1877) and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (circa 1881–1925).

Émile Durkheim (1858–1917) studied at École Normale Supérieure and under Wilhelm Wundt in Leipzig. He specialized in religious studies and other fields, holding professorships and posts at the University of Bordeaux, the Sorbonne, and École Pratique des Hautes Études.

Émile Senart (1847–1928) studied Indology and archaeology at Munich and Göttingen under Theodor Benfey. He taught as a professor at Collège de France and served as president of the Société Asiatique from 1908 to 1928.

Émile-Louis Burnouf (1821–1907) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at École Normale Supérieure and the University of Paris under Jean-Louis and Eugène Burnouf. He was a professor at Nancy (1854–1867) and director of École française d'Athènes (1867–1875).
Émilie Aussant is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Georges-Jean Pinault and held an attested post at Paris Diderot University in 2014.
Étienne Balazs (1905–1963) was a scholar of sinology and history. He studied under Otto Franke from 1923 to 1930 and held posts at the CNRS and the University of Paris starting in 1949.

Étienne Lamotte (1903–1983) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at KU Leuven and Paris under Louis de La Vallée Poussin and Sylvain Lévi. He was a long-time professor at KU Leuven and president of UCLouvain.
